clue.text: Dr rents big new building for Northern dramatist

indicators.note: a new building puts the bricks up afresh, so these letters are built again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A doctor lets out a large new building intended for a playwright from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new building' rearranges the ten letters of DR RENTS BIG. 'Northern' points to a Scandinavian: August Strindberg was Swedish.
explanation.definitionFit: August Strindberg, author of Miss Julie, was a Swedish playwright, so a dramatist from the North of Europe.

clue.text: Might be way up for good man with extended play

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated St
EP is the abbreviation for an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a good man who plays for longer is on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair or rung is one stage of a way up, so it might be a way up.

clue.text: Equip Dave anew for holy book

parts.note: to rig is to equip or fit out

indicators.note: made anew, so the name Dave is put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Dave is kitted out again to carry a sacred text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges DAVE into VEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rig Veda is the oldest of the Hindu scriptures, a collection of sacred hymns in Sanskrit.

clue.text: Not content with a conservative approach to writing, yet avoiding hard labour (in fact, thus disengaged)

definitions.text: Not content with a conservative approach to writing, yet avoiding hard labour (in fact, thus disengaged)

parts.words: Not content with a conservative approach to writing, yet avoiding hard labour (in fact, thus disengaged)
parts.note: a writer who rejects the Conservative line and also shuns hard-line Labour takes no side in party matters at all

explanation.surface: A writer unhappy with a cautious style who also dodges hard work is described as detached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not content' is the House of Lords' vote against; 'conservative' and 'labour' read as Britain's two main parties, Conservative and Labour, and someone siding with neither is detached from party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disengaged from party allegiance means standing outside politics.

clue.text: Scale devised by Sir Francis, heeding Defoe's earlier suggestion

definitions.text: Scale devised by Sir Francis, heeding Defoe's earlier suggestion

parts.words: Scale devised by Sir Francis, heeding Defoe's earlier suggestion
parts.note: Admiral Sir Francis gave his surname to the wind-force scale; Defoe had proposed grading winds in his book The Storm a century earlier

explanation.surface: A naval officer builds a measuring scale on an idea that Daniel Defoe had floated before him.
explanation.definitionFit: The wind-force scale running from calm to hurricane is named after the admiral Sir Francis who drew it up in 1805.

clue.text: Virginia's was common

parts.note: Virginia Woolf titled her essay collections The Common ___

explanation.surface: Something belonging to a woman named Virginia was ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like the US state; it is Virginia Woolf, whose essay collections are The Common Reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's book title pairs 'common' with the word for one who reads.

clue.text: Forster character just another graduate on the street

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A character from a novel is dismissed as just one more graduate living on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonard Bast is the struggling clerk in E. M. Forster's Howards End.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bast is a figure in E. M. Forster's novel Howards End.

clue.text: Girl with small child makes others face bare facts

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A girl and her little one force other people to confront the plain truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adamites were a sect who went naked in worship, so one makes others face bare facts in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Adamite sect practised nudity in imitation of Adam, so they present bare bodies to those around.

clue.text: Poetic apostrophe to frolic?

parts.note: Shelley's poem addresses a bird whose name as a verb means to frolic, so the title reads like 'to frolic'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a poem addressing play counts as a poetic apostrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostrophe here is a poem's direct address; Shelley's ode speaks to the bird, and to skylark also means to play about.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's famous ode is a direct poetic address to a songbird.

clue.text: Mere Augean clean-up from Bulwer Lytton's dominie

indicators.note: a clean-up rearranges what was there, so the letters of these two words are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Merely cleaning out the Augean stables is offered as the work of a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clean-up' plays on Hercules cleaning the Augean stables; it rearranges MERE AUGEAN. Bulwer Lytton's novel is about the murderer-schoolmaster Eugene Aram; a dominie is a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Aram, the real eighteenth-century schoolmaster hanged for murder, is the title figure of Bulwer Lytton's novel.

clue.text: Where Huxley's bad vision was worse than ever?

definitions.text: Where Huxley's bad vision was worse than ever?

parts.words: Where Huxley's bad vision was worse than ever?
parts.note: Aldous Huxley, who had poor sight, wrote Eyeless in ___, so that place is where vision failed entirely

explanation.surface: A question about where a near-blind author found his eyesight at its poorest.
explanation.walkthrough: Huxley's novel Eyeless in Gaza takes its title from Milton's Samson Agonistes; 'eyeless' is worse than bad vision.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Huxley's novel places its eyelessness in this Palestinian city.

clue.text: The Lord will provide a place in the land of Moriah

definitions.meaning: the Hebrew name means 'the Lord will provide'

definitions.text: a place in the land of Moriah
definitions.meaning: Abraham gave the name to the spot where he was spared sacrificing Isaac

explanation.surface: A promise of divine provision attached to a spot in the biblical land of Moriah.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis 22 Abraham names the mountain site in Moriah with a Hebrew phrase meaning that God sees to every need.

clue.text: Deceptively named Shakespearian heroine

indicators.note: the word heroine carries a male title within it, so the name sits concealed inside the word, deceptively

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine whose name gives the wrong idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deceptively named' points inside the word 'heroine', whose first four letters give the name; as a whole the clue describes Leonato's daughter in Much Ado About Nothing, whose name ordinarily means a valiant man.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonato's daughter in Much Ado About Nothing is a central female character with a masculine-sounding name.

clue.text: Jones's neighbour who deals with the animals

definitions.text: Jones's neighbour who deals with the animals

parts.words: Jones's neighbour who deals with the animals
parts.note: in Orwell's Animal Farm Mr Jones's neighbour, the farmer at Pinchfield, does business with the pigs

explanation.surface: The man next door to the Joneses who looks after livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Jones is the farmer ousted in Orwell's Animal Farm; his neighbour Frederick of Pinchfield cheats the animals in a timber deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick of Pinchfield Farm, beside Jones's Manor Farm, buys the animals' timber with forged banknotes.

clue.text: The Man that Corrupted Hadleyburg

parts.note: Mark Twain's story title; the vengeful stranger signs his letter with this surname

explanation.surface: The title of a Mark Twain story about a stranger who exposes a smug town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twain's story the stranger who brings the sack of gold signs himself Howard L. Stephenson.
explanation.definitionFit: The stranger who tempts the townsfolk of Hadleyburg uses the name Howard L. Stephenson.

clue.text: Grace on the road to encounter a lord of Antioch

indicators.note: in a down-the-page sense one piece placed on another comes before it in the word

parts.note: Thalia is one of the three Graces of Greek myth
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A graceful woman travels along the road to meet a nobleman of Antioch.
explanation.walkthrough: Thaliard is the lord sent by King Antiochus to kill Pericles in Shakespeare's Pericles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thaliard is the courtier of Antiochus, ruler of Antioch, in Shakespeare's Pericles.

clue.text: Imitations formed part of his work

definitions.text: Imitations formed part of his work

parts.words: Imitations formed part of his work
parts.note: the American poet Robert ___ published a book of free translations titled Imitations in 1961

explanation.surface: Someone's output is said to include copies of other people's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imitations' looks like plagiarism; it is the title of Robert Lowell's 1961 book of loose translations.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Lowell's collection Imitations, versions of European poems, won the Bollingen translation prize.

clue.text: His master a "wretched, rash, intruding fool

definitions.text: His master a "wretched, rash, intruding fool

parts.words: His master a "wretched, rash, intruding fool
parts.note: Hamlet calls Polonius a wretched, rash, intruding fool; the clue wants the servant Polonius sends to Paris

explanation.surface: Someone's employer is dismissed as a meddling idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's words over the body of Polonius; Reynaldo is the servant Polonius sends to spy on Laertes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reynaldo serves Polonius in Hamlet, the old counsellor Hamlet insults with these words.

clue.text: Wealthy widow of Belmont

parts.note: the rich lady of Belmont in The Merchant of Venice, left her fortune by her father

explanation.surface: A rich woman who has lost her husband and lives in Belmont.
explanation.walkthrough: Belmont is the estate of the heroine of The Merchant of Venice; 'widow' is loose, as she is an heiress left rich by her father.
explanation.definitionFit: The heiress of Belmont in The Merchant of Venice is courted for her riches.

clue.text: Possibly a louder virtuoso passage for Lear duo

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words a louder could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A louder showpiece might suit the two who sail off in Edward Lear's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges A LOUDER. Lear's Owl sings to the Pussycat in The Owl and the Pussycat, so a vocal flourish suits the duo.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rapid run of notes sung on one syllable, a showy vocal ornament.

clue.text: Article repairer holds for Greek comic playwright

indicators.note: holds means one word keeps another inside it

parts.note: a mender is someone who repairs things
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone who repairs things keeps a particular item for a Greek dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Menander was the leading writer of Athenian New Comedy in the fourth century BC.

clue.text: French novelist in single combat about bad actor

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two people
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A French writer fights a duel with a poor performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Duhamel wrote the Pasquier Chronicles and won the Prix Goncourt.

clue.text: Revolting Canaanite city, leftish politically, also (not applicable) hot

parts.note: Lib, short for Liberal, is a centre-left political label
H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap

explanation.surface: A disgusting ancient city is described as left-leaning and also sweltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting'; 2 Kings 8:22 says 'Then Libnah revolted', so it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Libnah was a Canaanite city taken by Joshua which later rebelled against the king of Judah.

clue.text: Jacks complete chap had one

parts.note: a complete person in the old sense of 'the compleat gentleman' is one who has received full schooling

explanation.surface: Every Jack who is a thoroughly rounded fellow had something.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and learning are what produce a fully formed, accomplished person.

clue.text: Ruler emulated by Mr Toad

parts.note: the Bible says this king of Israel drives furiously, as Toad of Toad Hall does in his motor car

explanation.surface: A king whose behaviour is copied by the toad in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 Kings 9:20 says 'the driving is like the driving of Jehu ... for he driveth furiously', and Mr Toad is a reckless motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jehu, king of Israel, is the Bible's proverbial furious driver.

clue.text: Masonic river's twofold existence

indicators.note: twofold means the same piece is written down twice

parts.note: is is the verb of existence, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A river with Masonic links is said to lead a double life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames at Oxford is called the Isis, and the Egyptian goddess Isis figures in Masonic lore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames at Oxford goes by the name of the Egyptian goddess revered in Masonic ritual.

clue.text: He doubled his capital in 70s work, before acceptable losses

definitions.text: He doubled his capital in 70s work, before acceptable losses

parts.words: He doubled his capital in 70s work, before acceptable losses
parts.note: a writer whose work of the 1870s doubled his fortune, read alongside a capitalised initial being doubled

explanation.surface: A man doubled his money with work in the seventies before taking tolerable losses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright, is the writer the clue describes.

clue.text: The animals were his brothers, so to speak

definitions.text: The animals were his brothers, so to speak

parts.words: The animals were his brothers, so to speak
parts.note: in Joel Chandler Harris's tales the animals are called Brer, a dialect form of 'brother', by the old storyteller

explanation.surface: A man regards all animals as his siblings, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' points to Brer, the spoken form of 'brother' in Brer Rabbit and Brer Fox.
explanation.definitionFit: The old narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's folk tales tells of Brer Rabbit, Brer Fox and Brer Bear.

clue.text: Festival doctor in the The Suicide Club

definitions.meaning: a name for the Christmas festival

definitions.text: doctor in the The Suicide Club
definitions.meaning: The physician in Stevenson's story The Suicide Club

explanation.surface: A party doctor turns up at a club for would-be suicides.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a word for Christmastide and the surname of the doctor in R. L. Stevenson's The Suicide Club.

clue.text: Emperor of the moon

parts.note: a Byzantine emperor's name that also belongs to a lunar crater

explanation.surface: A ruler of the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Theophilus was a ninth-century Byzantine emperor, and a large crater on the moon bears the name too.
